title: Sprint runs test in three tiers: narrow per task, the gate per landing, the heavy suites once at sprint end
goal: A kb-worker runs only its item's own -k checks plus ruff and tools_map, and the sync gate's tests.py --changed is the one mapped run per landing; backlog.py land no longer runs stress_test.py; the review story's checks run stress_test.py with the full tests.py once before review and retro; kb-sprint, kb-worker, kb-item and backlog.md state the three tiers.
notes: Tiers before the story: a worker runs the item's checks and tests.py --changed origin/main; land runs done, stress_test.py, rag.py eval and lint, then the sync gate runs --changed again; the review story runs the full tests.py once. After it: the worker runs no --changed, stress_test.py runs once at sprint end, and a red end run is bisected over the sprint's landings with its bug fixed by a worker dispatched at once. The story is large: /kb-item splits it into tasks (land and review checks; worker brief and docs; the bisect subcommand and the kb-sprint step). Mid-sprint heavy runs are scheduled by ST-t7xxgt47 from each landing's measured test impact; the bisect runs over the landings since the last heavy run and waits on ST-zkotxvdl's host lock. Each bisect step is recorded as an ops bisect.step row once the ops sidecar exists. The bisect clause and its three red_end_run checks were taken out of this story's goal when the operator dropped TK-qi7oo5l3 on 2026-10-04 (efficiency decision: with one agent and no unattended runs it has no measured pain); the sprint manager approved the narrowing.
